title: CMS Health Equity Strategy: From Aspiration to Requirement
summary: CMS's Framework for Health Equity, the Health Equity Index in Medicare Advantage Star Ratings, AHEAD model equity requirements, and Section 1557 non-discrimination obligations.

objectives.text: Describe the five priorities in CMS's Framework for Health Equity
Explain how the Health Equity Index affects Medicare Advantage Star Ratings
Summarize Section 1557 non-discrimination obligations for health care organizations

content_blocks.body: Health equity has moved from a voluntary aspiration to a regulatory requirement. CMS has embedded equity into payment programs, quality reporting, and plan contracting in ways that give health systems and payers financial and legal incentives to close disparities — not just acknowledge them.
content_blocks.heading: From voluntary to required

items.body: Expand collection of REaL and SDOH data across all CMS programs and require stratified reporting.

items.body: Build evidence on interventions that close disparities and share findings with the field.
items.title: Disparities research

items.title: Payment models

items.title: Cultural competency

content_blocks.heading: CMS Framework for Health Equity — 5 priorities

content_blocks.body: Beginning with the 2027 Star Ratings, CMS is introducing a Health Equity Index (HEI) reward that gives Medicare Advantage plans additional credit for improving quality for low-income and/or disabled enrollees. Plans that reduce disparities within their enrolled population are rewarded; those that perform worse for vulnerable subgroups are penalized. This is the first time equity performance has been directly linked to MA payment.
content_blocks.heading: Health Equity Index in Star Ratings

content_blocks.body:
Section 1557 of the ACA prohibits discrimination based on race, color, national origin, sex, age, and disability by any health program or activity receiving federal financial assistance — which includes virtually every hospital, health system, and insurer.

The 2024 Section 1557 final rule extended protections to LGBTQ+ individuals, required covered entities to provide meaningful access for people with limited English proficiency, and established requirements for accessible communication for people with disabilities. Health systems with federal funding must have a designated coordinator, a grievance procedure, and notice of nondiscrimination posted.
content_blocks.heading: Section 1557: Non-discrimination in health care
